content:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: rev d2f4 -> canary group A, initial traffic 10%. CI: green. link: https://deploys.redwood/rev/d2f4
incident-bot: Pager: P2 - elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (canary). triggered at 10:08Z
neha: @oncall-sre seeing 5xx ~3.5% on canary pods, latency also +120ms p95. Production customers hitting hosting endpoints.
neha: logs show `model-serving: kv-cache miss + OOM attempts` on canary nodes, only in region-us-west2.
tayler: can we immediately pause traffic shift? How stable is rollback?
sam: Reverting traffic from the routing layer should be safe. Two options: 1) flip routing back to baseline (fast) 2) flip feature flag (killflip) to disable new path (finer).
onchalant note: @frontend-eng noticed sticky sessions to canary due to session-cookie TTL; draining might be slow.
oncall-sre: @sam @neha I'm taking this. Starting manual rollback now. Posting steps I run so others know: 1) stop canary traffic shift, 2) toggle killflip flag to route requests to baseline, 3) drain canary pods, 4) run smoke curl checks.
sam: copy that. In flight: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` to verify.
deploy-bot: aborting further canary traffic increases. rollback command queued: `./deployctl traffic set canary 0 --group A`
neha: toggled killflip flag to OFF @featureflags (killflip -> false). Observed immediate drop in new canary sessions but existing sessions still routed.
marco: starting pod drain: `kubectl drain pod/canary-xyz --grace-period=60 --ignore-daemonsets` - found 12 active connections on one pod. Might be stuck due to long-running websocket connections.
frontend-eng: those websockets are sticky for some customers (chat preview). We should mark impacted customers and inform CS.
customer-success: hitting CS now - starting customer blast. Preliminary: ~4% of active hosted accounts in us-west2 saw degraded responses, most fallbacks succeeded. Collecting list of callers with elevated latency.
oncall-sre: drain progressing; 8/12 pods drained, remaining 4 have active conns > 90s. Forcible termination policy in 2m if they don't drop.
neha: observed error spike settle to baseline after killflip flip for new requests; ongoing errors come from long-lived sessions.
tayler: running smoke tests after routing flip:
```for i in {1..5}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE" https://canary-proxy.local/health || echo "fail $i"; sleep 1; done```
results: all healthy from baseline.
noncall-sre: forcible terminate remaining pods. Executed `kubectl delete pod/canary-abc --force --grace-period=0` for 2 pods. Error rate returned to baseline within 90s.
sam: verification checklist: - routing set to baseline (done) - killflip off (done) - pods drained/terminated (done) - smoke curl tests (ok) - perf dashboards normalized (p95 within 10% of baseline)
neha: metric snapshots: canary 5xx peaked at 3.8% -> baseline 0.18% after rollback; p95 latency from 420ms -> 300ms; request volume steady.
marco: posting quick logs from affected pod:
```
E 10:06 model-serving OOM when allocating KV cache size=1.2G; fallback to cpu path triggered; subsequent requests 500
W 10:07 websocket conn stalled for 95s
```
incident-bot: Incident set to "mitigated". Pager cleared.
customer-success: sent initial customer note to affected accounts, offered deeper troubleshooting; no major SLA breaches expected, flagging for follow-up.
tayler: next actions for postmortem: - capture exact canary config and kernel/quantization change in rev d2f4 - reproduce locally with kv cache small seed - propose traffic gating (prevent session-stick drift) - improve drain hooks for websockets
sam: I'll own reproducer + patch plan. @neha can you own dashboard alerts tuning so we catch kv-cache OOM earlier?
neha: on it, will set a canary-specific quota and an alert at 1% 5xx for canary group.
marco: small follow-up: consider setting session cookie diff on canary to reduce stickiness during early rollouts.
tayler: oncall handoff: @oncall-sre hands to @sam for follow-up tomorrow 09:00PT. No active customer impact.
customer-success: marking thread resolved for CS. Will update customers tomorrow with root cause once we have repro.
neha: thanks all. Closing this thread after we land reproducer. :thumbsup:
